experience.org: SFU Science Alive (Faculty of Applied Sciences Outreach)
bullets: Started and lead the program's internal web platforms, built with Claude Code: I set the requirements and priorities, and check each release against what staff need. Privacy rules for children: camper names become pseudonyms before anything is stored, and camper code runs apart from the main site.

Designed the AI workflow behind the build: Claude Code skills that take a request from board item to merged change, hooks that block risky actions, and specialized agents for building, review, and QA. Analyzed 365 AI-agent runs to find what drove cost and turn count, then changed brief limits and model settings from the results.
Launched *spark-gallery*, an online magazine of camper projects published each camp week: 509 projects from 471 campers through a full summer of camps.
Introduced *campkit*, a shared curriculum platform that replaced my earlier document pipeline, holding 356 activities and 25 camps for a six-person staff team.

Grew *hello-wattson* (hellowattson.ca) from an internal lesson site into a code-gated teaching platform for outside teachers that collects no student data: 22 programs, with an in-browser Arduino compiler and code playground.
Keep refining the platforms from feedback: triage problems reported by writers and instructors into tracked issues, document them, and decide what ships next.
Wrote SPARK, the program's workshop-design framework; teach coding camps (Python, web, Arduino, LEGO robotics).
Built a Java JSON response builder for API validation and generated Java bindings from Thrift IDLs, integrating them with Wiremock containers for test stubs.
Implemented a single source of truth for regression tests using the Trino REST API.
Wrote automated GUI tests in Java and Selenium and set up a Docker + Jenkins continuous-testing environment.

Built the human-move detection module with a Raspberry Pi camera and OpenCV, comparing board states to identify the moved piece; drove an electromagnetic trolley in Python to execute the machine's moves.
